meta.note: Supply only. 2026 = harvest to date plus the rest of the year at the same pace; 2027 = our harvest projection times the 6 kg+ share expected, low and high cases in brackets.

basins.name: Norway
basins.how: Harvest (1,537 kt in 2025, 1,630 kt in 2026) × share of 6 kg+ in the harvest from Sjømat Norge's weekly size report (11.9 % in 2025, 15.7 % so far in 2026). 2027: our generations model, 6 kg+ harvested January–September 2027 against the same months of 2026: +20 % central (+2 % if the new generation loses its growth advance, +30 % if it keeps all of it).
known: Fish over 5 kg at sea at the end of September: 52 kt gutted against 39 kt a year earlier (+34 %).
The generation being harvested grows 14 % faster per fish and loses 0.85 % of its fish a month (1.43 % a year earlier).
Next generation: 283 M fish at 1.07 kg (289 M at 1.00 kg a year earlier).
October 2026: 14.5 % of the harvest in 6 kg+ (13.1 % a year earlier), from harvest-boat visits.
up: The new generation keeps its growth advance: a wave of 6 kg+ in spring–summer 2027 (+30 % case).
Low mortality and fewer lice treatments let farmers keep fish longer.
down: Algae (spring 2026 in the south, 2025 in the north), ISA or a jellyfish year force early harvests of smaller fish.
Weak premium for big sizes pushes farmers to harvest earlier.
Norway is at its legal biomass limit: more 6 kg+ means fewer small fish, not more salmon.

basins.name: Chile
basins.how: Atlantic harvest (724 kt in 2025, 740 kt in 2026) × share of 6 kg+ estimated from the average harvest weight reported by Camanchaca and Multi X (5.17 kg live in 2025, 5.02 kg in 2026Q1; estimated share 20 % and 16 %, assuming the usual spread of weights). Customs confirm the direction: 6 kg+ were 35 % of the whole Atlantic salmon exported over the last six months against 42 % a year earlier. 2027: harvest -2.1 % at the 2026 weight; low case: harvest -9 % and 0.3 kg lighter fish; high case: harvest +1 % and back to 2025 weights.
known: Standing biomass about 7 % below a year earlier; harvest slowing since August.
Record El Niño: Chilean sea 1–3 °C above normal; preventive algae emergency from 1 Nov 2026 to 30 Jun 2027.
Sea lice at a high (65 farms above the threshold in Q3 2026); SRS causes 53 % of infectious mortality (2025) and forced early harvests at Camanchaca in Q1 2026.
FOB price of 6 kg+ up 16 % in Q3 2026 as volumes fell.
up: A mild algae season and calmer El Niño let farmers grow fish to full size.
Fewer early harvests for lice and SRS.
down: A bloom like 2016 or 2021 in the inner seas (Los Lagos, Aysén) or new losses in Magallanes.
Warm water speeds growth but pushes farmers to harvest early, at smaller sizes, to limit risk.
Companies changing hands (Blumar sold to Agrosuper) may change harvest plans.

basins.name: Faroe Islands
basins.how: Harvest (115 kt in 2025, 136 kt in 2026) × share of 6 kg+ estimated from Bakkafrost's average harvest weight (gutted): 5.7 kg in H1 2026 against 5.1 kg in H1 2025, back to 5.0 kg in Q3 2026 (estimated share 39 % in 2025, 46 % in 2026, assuming the usual spread of weights). 2027: flat harvest (Bakkafrost plans as much as in 2026) at the 2025 weight; low case 4.9 kg, high case 5.6 kg.
known: H1 2026 was a big-fish half-year: 5.7 kg on average against 5.1 kg a year earlier; Q3 2026 back to 5.0 kg.

Bakkafrost Faroes harvest guidance 2026: 97,000 t (raised from 92,000 t in May); smolts put to sea in 2026: 9.5 million in H1, 4.5 million in Q3; average smolt weight 527 g in Q1 2026 (449 g in 2025).
SEB on Q2 2026: heavier fish (5.6 kg vs 5.0 kg) but the premium for larger fish remained limited.
up: Larger smolts (527 g in Q1 2026) and good biology let fish reach 6 kg+ again in 2027.
down: The H1 2026 bulge came from one strong generation; the fish harvested since July are lighter.
Bakkafrost may harvest earlier if the premium for big fish stays small.

basins.name: Iceland
known: Fish over 5 kg at sea in 2026-09: 6.4 kt against 10.6 kt a year earlier (-40 %); 4–5 kg: 7.4 kt against 9.2 kt (MAST).

basins.name: Scotland
known: Scottish farmers harvested early in 2026 because of gill disease and mortality (Scottish Sea Farms cut its 2026 harvest guidance by 3,000 t; Bakkafrost Scotland ended external smolt sourcing after biological setbacks). Bakkafrost Scotland harvest weight: 6.4 kg in Q1 2026, 5.2 kg in Q2 (4.4 kg in June). No national size statistics.

lead: 6 kg+ salmon from Norway, Chile and the Faroes: about 438 kt in 2026 (+17 % on 2025) and 480 kt in 2027 (+9 %, range 361–555 kt). Norway drives the change; more big fish in Norway; fewer in Faroe Islands, Iceland, Scotland.
